label: Ivy League
definition: The eight members of the Ivy League.

label: Ivy Plus
definition: Ivy-Plus = the eight Ivy League colleges plus the University of Chicago, Duke University, MIT and Stanford University (12 colleges), as defined by Chetty, Deming & Friedman (Opportunity Insights). Listed here: the four non-Ivy members only.
source: Chetty, R., Deming, D.J., Friedman, J.N. 'Diversifying Society's Leaders? The Determinants and Causal Effects of Admission to Highly Selective Private Colleges', NBER Working Paper 31492 (2023; revised Aug 2025). https://opportunityinsights.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/CollegeAdmissions_Paper.pdf ; https://www.nber.org/papers/w31492

label: Public Ivies
definition: The 30 universities profiled in Howard R. Greene & Matthew W. Greene, The Public Ivies: America's Flagship Public Universities (New York: Cliff Street Books/HarperCollins, 2001; ISBN 0-06-093459-X). Main campus only (see _meta.campusScope).
source: Greene & Greene (2001), ISBN 0-06-093459-X. List as transcribed at https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Ivy (section 'Greenes' Guides list (2001)') and corroborated at https://www.bestcolleges.com/blog/public-ivy-schools-and-little-ivies/ . The book itself was not inspected; the two secondary sources may not be independent.

label: Little Ivies
definition: The 18 colleges shown as 'Little Ivies' in the Bloomberg Businessweek chart 'Prestige Can't Buy Performance' accompanying McDonald & Smith, 'Little Good News for the Little Ivies', Bloomberg Businessweek, 22 Dec 2016.
source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-12-22/little-good-news-for-the-little-ivies (archived: https://web.archive.org/web/20170201234955/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2016-12-22/little-good-news-for-the-little-ivies ; chart image: https://assets.bwbx.io/images/users/iqjWHBFdfxIU/iVbPvJL9p4qs/v0/-1x-1.png). Article text: 'a group of 18 liberal arts schools sometimes dubbed "Little Ivies"'. This is the list used by https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Little_Ivies .
